items.scope: End of life open source projects supported by HeroDevs if hosted on HeroDevs.com, or issues in open source projects discovered by or reported to HeroDevs, unless covered by the scope of another CNA.
Vulnerabilities in any Google Cloud developed product and not under the scope of another CNA.
All Proofpoint products.
All Honeywell products.
All EnterpriseDB products and vulnerabilities identified in open source libraries used by EnterpriseDB products unless covered by another CNA’s scope.
AxxonSoft products and solutions, Abetechs GmbH products and solutions (GRUNDIG security products, and C-WERK software solutions).
All upKeeper Solutions products, excluding end-of-life (EOL) as listed in the upKeeper Solutions End of Life Policy.
TIBCO issues only.
Ericsson issues only.
Danfoss products only.
Mautic core and officially supported plugins.
Delta Electronics products as listed on www.deltaww.com.
All Acronis products, including Acronis Cyber Protect, Acronis Cyber Protect Home Office, Acronis DeviceLock DLP, and Acronis Snap Deploy.
Vulnerabilities in the following Altium products only: Altium Designer, A365, Octopart, and Altium Enterprise Server.
Vulnerabilities in Snyk products and vulnerabilities discovered by, or reported to, Snyk that are not in another CNA’s scope.
All Esri products only, including ArcGIS.
Projects within The Document Foundation only, e.g., LibreOffice, LibreOffice Online; The Document Foundation discourages reporting denial of service bugs as security issues.
All Qualys products and vulnerabilities discovered by Qualys that are not covered by another CNA’s scope.
Vulnerability assignment related to its vulnerability coordination role.
Kaspersky B2C and B2B products, as well as vulnerabilities discovered in third-party software not in another CNA’s scope.
ASR products only.
Vulnerabilities in third-party products discovered by ZUSO ART that are not in another CNA’s scope.
Pegasystems products only.

CVEs requested by code owners using the GitHub Security Advisories feature and vulnerabilities affecting open source projects discovered by security researchers at GitHub or Microsoft not covered by another CNA’s scope.

All Wind River branded products as found on windriver.com including vulnerabilities in natively developed or modified product incorporated components, and only product incorporated third-party components not in another CNA’s scope.
Citrix issues only.
LG Electronics products only.
N-able branded products and technologies only.
Vulnerabilities related to products of Mitsubishi Electric Group.
All dotCMS product services including the vulnerabilities reported in our open source core located at https://github.com/dotCMS/core.
Zephyr project components, and vulnerabilities that are not in another CNA’s scope.

Vulnerabilities in Delinea products or services listed on delinea.com, or vulnerabilities in third-party products or services discovered by or reported to Delinea, unless covered by the scope of another CNA.
Vulnerability assignment related to FSI’s vulnerability coordination role in the South Korea financial sector that are not in another CNA’s scope.

Vulnerabilities that are discovered, validated, and coordinated through the Hackrate Ethical Hacking Platform, including: software, web applications, APIs, and cloud services; vulnerabilities validated and triaged by our internal security team; and findings disclosed under our coordination that are not in another CNA’s scope.
All Ribose products and services, including open source projects, supported products, and end-of-life/end-of-service products.
All ConnectWise products and services and vulnerabilities discovered by ConnectWise in third party products that are not within another CNA’s scope.
Lexmark products only.

Root Scope: European Union (EU) member states/EU authorities, EU CSIRTs network members, and cooperative partners under ENISA’s mandate as well as other CNAs who choose ENISA as their Root.

CNA Scope: Vulnerabilities in information technology (IT) products discovered by European Union (EU) Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) or reported to EU CSIRTs for coordinated disclosure, as long as they do not fall under a CNA with a more specific scope.

Vulnerability coordination for vulnerabilities in all products reported to CERT-In in accordance with our vulnerability coordination role as a CERT. Vulnerability assignments for vulnerabilities impacting all products designed, developed, and manufactured in India.
Microchip Technology products only.

All Cisco products, and any third-party research targets that are not in another CNA’s scope. Cisco will not issue a CVE ID for issues reported on products that are past the Last Day of Support milestone, as defined on Cisco’s End-of-Life Policy, which is available at https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/eos-eol-policy.html.
Qualcomm and Snapdragon issues only.
Juniper issues only.
Switzerland Government Common Vulnerability Program.

Vulnerabilities in open source projects affecting the Fedora Project, that are not covered by a more specific CNA. CVEs can be assigned to vulnerabilities affecting end-of-life or unsupported releases by the Fedora Project.
Vulnerabilities in software discovered by DIVD, and vulnerabilities reported to DIVD for coordinated disclosure, which are not in another CNA’s scope.
All HCL products only.
MongoDB products only, not including end-of-life components or products.
Azure Access branded products and technologies only.
Zabbix products and Zabbix projects listed on https://git.zabbix.com/ only.
